sections.body:
# Production review

Observe the actual artifact before comparing it with the commission and applicable sources. Record the evaluation and any actual repair or selection decision against that artifact. The author can perform this review; independent evaluation has a separately established input boundary.

## Review, disposition and selection

Production owns the evaluation and disposition of its candidates.
The Studio reads the same records; its iteration ledger keeps the candidate identity, media references and adoption history, not another verdict.

```sh
python scripts/production_workflow.py draft-review --root STUDIO --run RUN --candidate CANDIDATE --out review.json
python scripts/production_workflow.py review --root STUDIO --run RUN --file review.json
python scripts/production_workflow.py draft-disposition --root STUDIO --run RUN --candidate CANDIDATE --out disposition.json
python scripts/production_workflow.py disposition --root STUDIO --run RUN --file disposition.json
python scripts/production_workflow.py candidate-status --root STUDIO --run RUN --candidate CANDIDATE
```

`candidate-status`, Studio candidate displays and sheet inventory report the
formal evaluation and disposition from the run's registered input records
and current event history. They check the evidence that supports those
decisions. `production_workflow.py status --run RUN` also audits every
published input and compiled request and reports execution readiness.
Mutations acquire their own complete current run before applying a decision.
Operations that require authorization also check current authority at their
effect boundary; a displayed selection grants no permission to perform those
actions.

A review names the actual reviewer, observations, the criteria assessed so far, optional supplemental `evidence`, repairs, unresolved matters and a conclusion.
Each observation names its `evidence` (`candidate`, an automatic comparison evidence ID or a supplemental evidence ID), a locator, the observed fact, its interpretation and limitations.
Additional evidence entries record path, kind, relation and limitations; their bytes are measured and pinned, not trusted from filenames.

`workspace --phase review` and the `draft-review` report include `review_guide`.
The workspace summary owns those evidence entries once under `evidence`;
the draft guide and full workspace use `review_guide.automatic_evidence`.
Those entries identify the actual candidate with the reserved ID
`candidate` and lists the retained comparison sources with their exact IDs,
media kinds and paths. Use those IDs directly in `observations[].evidence`.
The candidate event digest in `review.candidate` is a separate identifier.
Keep `review.evidence` for additional sources: do not redeclare automatic
evidence there. A copy of the candidate PNG under a new supplemental ID does
not replace an observation citing `candidate`.

The guide's `observation_template` supplies the entry shape with the observation
and interpretation unanswered. Write the facts you actually observed, the
meaning you judge from them, and the limits of that inspection. For a source
comparison, add a separate observation using that source's displayed evidence
ID. In each check, `observation_indices` cites zero-based positions in the
complete `observations` array. `criterion_citations` names each criterion's
required medium and whether a passing identity check must cite the candidate.
Use a measured stream and the interval actually inspected for motion or audio;
a whole-file label does not establish either.

`draft-review --out FILE` still saves only the editable review form to `FILE`.
Its standard summary contains `draft_file`, the exact candidate binding,
`review_guide`, unanswered locations and the concrete `next_action`.
`--view full` includes `choices`, the same form. Fill the saved form
from actual observations, then invoke that next action with the same file.
Guide templates and artifact decoding supply no finding or passing verdict.

The review workspace keeps every criterion and its authored relationships.
Read applicable original sources at `sources[].saved_path` and `evidence[].path`
using their declared scopes and locators. Source bodies are not copied into each
workspace response. The complete structural identity map and other selected
prepared context have exact `full_report` locations, while the summary retains
identity bindings, whole-subject obligations and every unresolved finding.
Open those originals and relationships whenever they are needed for judgment;
their displayed locations supply no reading or review result.

`saved_knowledge` locates the model, selected offering and guide resources
retained with the prepared request. Read those originals for model-specific
interpretation and limitations. The operation reading supplies the current
review contract without substituting a later catalog edition for that input.

`draft-review` remembers the chosen output path and its exact run, candidate
and preceding review. After interruption, status points to that same file while
its basis remains current, including when the file is still being edited.
Several saved drafts are explicit alternatives. Their answers do not change
the candidate or its independent review workspace; the `review` command checks
the completed file before recording it. Authored revisions use the same draft
discovery and apply the file with `review-authored`.

Review the commissioned criteria. An image evidence kind names the medium; it
does not create an artistic-quality requirement. For a technical enlargement,
decode the returned file and measure its dimensions against the requested
factor. Compare it with the source for any commissioned preservation or identity
requirement. Dimensions alone do not establish fidelity or visual quality.
Record supported findings and limits, then follow the selection and completion
actions for the actual task. Excluding an artistic-quality comparison does not
prevent a technical review from being completed.

### Observe before interpreting

First inspect the actual candidate and record what it visibly or measurably
establishes, with locators and limits. When a separate independent review is
part of the task, give that reviewer the candidate and technical information needed to
access the relevant file, page, region or stream. Withhold the brief, prompt,
expected portrayal, earlier failures and production history until that first
observation is recorded. `workspace --phase observe --candidate CANDIDATE` supplies only the saved candidate bytes, their access paths and measured media information. Give that view alone to the first observer. The later `workspace --phase review --candidate CANDIDATE` supplies the assessment basis. Even the compact editing draft contains criterion identifiers, so keep it out of the first observer's input.

Then compare the observed depiction with the commissioned result and applicable
source or reference evidence. Use the prepared criteria and allowed variation
within that authority. Additional inspection may answer a
criterion-specific question; keep those later observations distinguishable from
the first reading in their `limitations`. Preserve the direct observation in
`observation`, its meaning against the criterion in `interpretation`, and the
unsupported or uninspected scope in `limitations`. Record the actual reviewer
input boundary and reading order in the review's `conclusion` and relevant
observation limitations. These existing fields require no new record format.

For a visual construction, begin with the whole viewing experience and the
relationships that produce it. Observe the large shapes and intervals, spatial
or graphic organization, degree of exaggeration, rendering behavior, and the
way content holds together. Follow a consequential relationship into detail
when needed. Describe what the image actually invites the viewer to see before
checking whether named text, lights, props or other expected parts appear.
Their presence can coexist with a substantially different kind of picture.
Read crossings within that whole pattern: which mass interrupts another, what
remains inferable, and how that changes pressure, depth or attention. Separate
checking of a face, word and background can favor unobstructed displays while
missing their intended interference. A hidden feature is not automatically a
defect, nor is additional overlap automatically an improvement. Assess the
commissioned relationship and its actual degree.

Read color in the same connected way: where broad tones join different objects,
where chroma is concentrated or withheld, and where shadow, light, line and
printed surface use different treatments. Matching hue names or finding the
right costume colors does not establish the same distribution or representation.

Inspect at the scale the judgment requires. A whole-image view can establish
composition while leaving a small connection, boundary or count unresolved.
When that detail decides a criterion, inspect the available original pixels or
an appropriate region while retaining enough surrounding context to understand
the relationship. A crop or enlargement helps only when it reveals relevant
evidence; it cannot establish detail absent from the source. Record a supported
verdict when the evidence resolves the claim, and retain `indeterminate` when it
does not.

If the same context produced and reviewed the work, state that this is author
self-review and not independent. Describe the artifact before applying the
expected reading, while retaining the limitation that the intent is already
known. An instruction to forget that intent does not erase it. Input-limited
review also remains an interpretation, not a controlled blind comparison; the
[Blind Image Evaluation Protocol](../blind-image-evaluation-protocol.md) owns
study design and release claims.

A face oriented toward someone does not alone show eye contact; cropped eyes
can leave it undecided. A still stance does not establish a path of motion, and
a smile alone need not distinguish the requested emotional state or the
individual's selected way of expressing it. Observe the actual channel
relationships before assigning an emotional description. Assess the artifact
against what its evidence can establish. Use `indeterminate` for an
inspected criterion with inconclusive evidence and `not-assessed` for one not
inspected. Do not infer a pass from the prompt, the intended story or a valid
request. A valid prompt and a rejected candidate can coexist. A different
composition may pass when it preserves the same anchors and allowed variation.

For close reconstruction or a scoped transfer, compare the original and the
candidate as complete constructions at comparable viewing sizes. Assess the
commission's allowed changes separately from departures in the relationships
that carry the source. General appeal, readable copy or a usable object cannot
compensate for losing a required organization of the picture. Conversely, a
source's incidental weakness is not an improvement requirement unless the
commission assigns it one. Keep fidelity to supplied prompt text distinct
from fidelity to the actual sample when those sources differ. Explain the
overall match and the decisive differences; a checklist or average score does
not replace that judgment. Extracted criteria must not narrow the original
commission to the few qualities the author chose to describe.
For a whole-picture example, an unmentioned feature is not automatically an
allowed loss of its visual function. Separate compatible subject matter from
correspondence of construction, and justify consequential changes at the scope
the actual commission delegates.

### Apply the prepared review basis

Read each hard criterion's declared `origin` and `observation` beside the actual
request and selected source. A direct emotion such as happiness is assessable
as an impression; the image does not certify the subject's actual inner state.
Assess the simultaneous visible configuration of a still, and use an applied
baseline for a comparison. A sequence of panels may show ordering but not prove
elapsed duration. Motion or audio criteria require the corresponding measured
evidence; a video container alone does not establish that it carries audio.

Keep an agent's staging or appendage choice advisory unless actual instruction
or adoption requires it. A source example retains its conditions and variation;
it does not become a universal rule. Secondary figurative impressions and
necessary scene context cannot serve as literal hard proof. Check whether the
impression obscures the primary depiction, and retain uncertainty explicitly.
Mechanical validation checks declarations and references. It cannot establish
that an origin label is truthful or that prose and images communicate the
declared meaning. Correct a mistaken criterion at its current authored owner
and prepare a new revision; preserve saved images, reviews and earlier runs.

Assess the selected appearance goal and applicable source scope. Keep observed
facial proportions, physique, posture, clothing and relationships distinct from
unobserved facts about age, health, psychology or history. A youthful-looking
result does not establish a canonical age, and an appearance mismatch does not
pass merely because a background label seems to agree with it. Compare the
actual forms and permitted variation. Do not infer or rewrite canonical facts
from image classification, keywords or the success of a control term. Term and
weight choices are means; their correctness alone cannot pass the image.
Use the existing observation, interpretation and limitations fields, following
[Production direction](production-direction.md#translate-established-facts-into-the-current-appearance).

Applied task sources are available at their captured bytes as
`task-source:SOURCE_ID`, including the actual current request retained by
[Authoring work](authoring-work.md). Read that request and the applied source
roles beside the chosen purpose, direction and criteria. Work goals locate the
task; previous requests and candidates retain their comparison roles.
An agent's earlier direction is a proposed means; the authored review basis
names it `source_task_direction` and its checks `source_task_criteria`. It
remains available for comparison without becoming the user's commission.

For a materialized JSON source selection, `task-source:SOURCE_ID` supplies the
currently applied content and `source-origin:SOURCE_ID` supplies the complete
acquired original. Read the selected scope and compare it with that original;
other original values remain context. The compiler derives the task source's
`origin` path and hash from its acquisition. Its derived `applications` retains
each selected `pointer`, assigned `subjects` and `requirement` under its own
application `id`. Read those individual relationships when several characters
use different parts of one original. Canonical identity authority keeps its
own metadata.

For image inputs, the review workspace includes the original source images and each prepared delivery carrier available in the run. Carrier evidence retains
the source assignment, transformation, attachment position and board region;
external inputs also retain the exact request field. Several logical
references may share one saved carrier while keeping their individual
authority scopes. Compare the candidate against the image and region that
carry each requested attribute, and use the original source to assess what
the preparation preserved. Missing or changed saved bytes fail integrity
validation. The submission evidence separately establishes whether those
prepared inputs were sent.

The review workspace presents the prepared purpose and intended effect once,
followed by each criterion's evidence kind, current expression and realization,
and applicable entries from `direction.source_allowances`. The editing draft contains unanswered observations and verdicts, with empty reasons. Write the actual judgment there. Its `evidence` list is for additional authored sources; the runtime resolves prepared source and carrier evidence automatically, using the stable IDs shown in the workspace. The formal review retains all effective evidence and its saved bytes. Source records establish what was commissioned; observations
establish what the candidate supplies. Assess the chosen realization and the
returned result against the commission and applicable source requirements.
Accept a suitable alternative that meets those requirements; assess the actual
effect when a renderer follows choices that miss the request. Review the basis
of a mistaken criterion in the same assessment and revise the responsible task
through its existing authority before formal selection. Preserve inherited
identity, necessary use conditions and the scope of any authorized local edit
when correcting a criterion grounded only in the author's chosen means.
Keep uncertainty about an unsupported judgment in the review's limitations.
An intentionally ambiguous portrayal is itself assessable when the artifact
requests it. Changes to a live task leave this prepared review basis unchanged.

For adopted identity sources, the `decision` and `review` workspaces include
the frozen `identity_coverage` report in their assessment basis. It preserves original
values, grouped selections, subject scope and original authority, explicit
scene treatments and their exact text or media carriers. Unbound source values
remain comparison context rather than a list of parts to expose or exclude. Original source bytes
remain available as `identity-source:SOURCE_ID` evidence, including sources
derived from selected state or reference owners. The report is comparison
context, not a verdict; the editing draft still begins unassessed. Neither the
candidate-only `observe` view nor the blind `input` view includes this context.
When source scopes share the same original bytes, the workspace includes that
original text once. Later scopes name its first source ID in `content_ref`
while keeping their own scope, pointer and saved access path.

Use the applicable original definitions, conditions and relations to establish
the character being depicted, including requirements inherited by this scene.
Assess each required whole-subject criterion against that source independently
of the prepared prompt and extracted checks. Compare the selected current
portrayal with those requirements as well: a prompt that changes the individual
does not become the definition merely because the image follows it. Record a
supported pass when the candidate preserves the adopted construction and the
current portrayal's required meaning and features within their permitted
variation. A different suitable realization can meet those requirements;
membership in the same broad emotion or pose category does not establish that
it does. Retain the original definition for
`not-exposed` and `not-applicable` scopes, with the scene treatment and visibility
limits in the existing observations and reasons. Assess discrepancies and
uncertain details by their effect on the applicable identity requirements and
selection. Keep nonblocking uncertainty in observations, reasons or limitations
and optional improvements in proposed repairs. Use `unresolved` for issues that
need resolution or explicit owner acceptance before selection, including
findings beyond the extracted criteria. A necessary repair describes the
construction or relationship the revised result should show at the affected scope.

For conditional character performance, use the concrete response definition in
the applicable persona, under [Character Performance](character-performance.md),
and the selected condition and degree, with the depicted moment where relevant.
Review the visible relationships among the relevant gaze, expression, physiology,
appendages, posture, support, hands, distance, contact or other declared
channels. Include the whole configuration where it carries the response; a
local smile can coexist with an incompatible posture or addressed target.
Account for display control, deliberate concealment and held channels from the
definition. Hidden feeling need not become a visible cue. State which required
relationships the image establishes and which the framing leaves unobserved.

Apply the meaning and variation established before inspecting the result.
For example, if a portrayal requires eyes held open while the gaze turns away,
closed eyes do not become equivalent merely because either face can be called
embarrassed. If eye opening is left within the permitted range, assess whether
the actual gaze, mouth, bodily configuration and context preserve the required
response. Natural differences in rendering or wording can satisfy that same
definition. Do not make every prompt term a fixed feature, or relax an actual
fixed feature into an emotion label to accommodate the output. A specified
ambiguous or quiet performance has its own intended construction and range;
an unresolved authoring choice does not establish such an intention.

A useful unexpected expression can be proposed as another design or current
portrayal. Assess that proposal at its owning definition or Production direction
before using it under a revised basis. Its appeal does not retrospectively
establish the earlier intent, an unrecorded conditional rule or a passing
review. An owner's acceptance of a recorded departure leaves the observation
and verdict intact and supplies no new permanent mannerism. Preserve earlier
inputs and reviews when a revised source or selected portrayal needs new work.

A passing identity criterion must cite the actual candidate in its required
medium. An effective `unresolved` binding blocks a pass for its criterion and
the affected subjects' whole-identity criteria; resolve its owning source or
scene choice in a newly prepared input, or retain the actual nonpassing
assessment. More specific authored treatments determine the effective scope.
Omitting a required whole-subject check, or leaving it `not-assessed`, cannot
permit selection or be waived as an assessed departure. A supported
whole-subject pass remains limited to the depicted identity that this scene's
evidence establishes.

Locators are `whole`; `description` with text; one-based inclusive `lines` or `bytes`; `image-region` with normalized x, y, width and height; or `time`.
A `time` locator names an integer stream index and decimal-string `start_seconds` and `end_seconds` within that measured stream.
A motion check needs a nonzero video interval, and audio needs an audio stream.
Neither whole-file labels nor two still images prove the motion between them.
Text or binary evidence cannot pass an image check.

Each criterion gets one verdict:

- `pass` cites observations that support the criterion's declared evidence kind;
- `fail` records a decisive failure, which may come before other criteria are assessed;
- `indeterminate` means the reviewer observed the criterion and could not decide; it cites observations like `pass` and `fail`;
- `not-assessed` leaves the criterion unassessed and permits an empty reason; every judged verdict needs a reason. `not-applicable` excludes the criterion with its explanation.

The candidate's latest review sets its evaluation, by the first row that applies:

| Latest review | Evaluation |
|---|---|
| none, or every criterion `not-assessed` | `unreviewed` (the review reference is kept) |
| any `fail` | `nonconforming` |
| any `indeterminate`, or an unresolved issue listed | `indeterminate` |
| some criteria not assessed | `partially_reviewed` |
| every criterion `pass` or `not-applicable` | `conforming` |

These labels summarize all recorded criteria, including advisory ones. They
do not decide selection eligibility. An advisory failure or an inconclusive
advisory observation can coexist with supported passes on every hard criterion.
Keep the limitation and any optional repair visible rather than changing its
verdict to obtain a preferred aggregate label. The owner's explicit acceptance
can permit selection of assessed departures or uncertainties under the rules
below; the candidate keeps its actual evaluation.

Disposition is a separate axis: `pending`, `not_selected`, or `selected`, from the candidate's latest decision event.
A disposition file allows `pending` and `not_selected`; only `select` establishes `selected`.
Not selecting a candidate says nothing about its quality.
After completion, `not_selected` can retire an existing candidate that the
Studio no longer holds as its accepted image. The run retains its original
completion and owning task state. A later disposition of the delivered
candidate withdraws its current selection for further adoption; completion
verification still checks the selection and evidence recorded when the run
completed. Repeating the same disposition returns its existing receipt.
Returning a candidate to `pending`, recording another review or selection,
and starting new production require an open run. Abandoned runs keep their
existing closed decision policy.
Each review event names the review it follows in `previous_review`, and submitting the latest review again records nothing.
A synthetic candidate rejected on one failed criterion, with the other left unassessed (trimmed):

```json
{
  "candidate": "43c4d65069b4...", "candidate_sha256": "d035bda74f89...",
  "evaluation": "nonconforming", "disposition": "not_selected", "unassessed_criteria": ["output"],
  "review": "7a64a5f4e4dd...", "decision": "4f422dc3f32d...",
  "reviewed_at": "2026-10-03T19:02:37Z", "decided_at": "2026-10-03T19:02:44Z",
  "selection_current": null, "selection_diagnostics": []
}
```

`selection_current` is true or false for a selected candidate and null otherwise.
`selection_diagnostics` names `SELECTION_REVIEW_CHANGED` or `SELECTION_REPLACED` when a selection is not current.
`status` reports the same states for every candidate.
`selection_basis` distinguishes `review-pass` from `owner-allowance`, and
`owner_acceptance` exposes the recorded allowance. `selection_requirements`
retains the latest review's `unassessed_hard_criteria`,
`nonpassing_hard_criteria` and `unresolved_indices`; acceptance does not erase
those findings.

## Review, repair and a new run

The same review carries repairs (`id`, decision IDs, observation indices, operation, changed targets, reason).
Identify the responsible layer from the observations before choosing the
operation. [Production direction](production-direction.md#observe-and-repair)
connects the criterion, construction, presentation and rendition. A wrong
temporal phase or spatial relationship can require rebuilding the scene; an
incidental facial or garment edit cannot establish an event the view cannot
show. Use a local correction when the mismatch is local, and retain uncertainty
when the evidence does not isolate a cause.

For a saved authored artifact, follow
[Edit and save](production-authored-storage.md#edit-and-save): open
`draft-inputs --from-run REVISION --operation amend`, edit the retained choices,
then follow the owning plan's `advance` or the standalone `save` action. This
publishes a new authored revision while preserving the earlier revision and its
records. Its saved-artifact digest is distinct from a generated candidate-event
digest. The `revision-intent` and `revise` commands below repair a reviewed
generated candidate selected by its candidate-event digest.

Draft from the source run, edit the responsible authored choices and build
the revised task. Preserve the earlier input and candidate evidence.
`revision-intent` compares the whole prepared input, checks the reviewed scope, and returns an exact `edit` payload:

```text
python scripts/production_workflow.py revision-intent --root STUDIO --run RUN --task revised-task.json --candidate CANDIDATE --repair REPAIR_ID
python scripts/production_workflow.py revise --root STUDIO --run RUN --task revised-task.json --candidate CANDIDATE --repair REPAIR_ID --authorization EDIT_AUTHORIZATION
```

Authorize the returned edit intent, then `revise` creates a new run linked to the parent candidate, latest review, repair and exact changed input.
The edit record of the parent run reserves the new run's ID before preparation starts.
Running the same `revise` again returns that run with `formal_run_created: false` and prepares nothing; after an interruption before publication it publishes the reserved run.
When another preparation has registered a run under the reserved ID with another parent, `revise` reports `INPUT_CONSISTENCY_ERROR` with that run in `child`; both records stay, and a new authorization of the same edit intent records another edit, which reserves a new ID.
The new run needs its own direction and submit authorization and real evidence.
Its preparation transfers none of the parent's passing checks or permission to send.
Changed approval evidence requires new authority, not a repair that grants itself more power.

## Deterministic pixel realization

Read [Image Editing](image-editing.md) for the `image-edit` feature.
Its exact intent binds the plan, pinned input pixels, latest reviewed repair and new PNG path to an existing edit authorization.
This creates a candidate in the current run, not a new selected direction or an inherited review.
Contract changes still use `revision-intent` and `revise`.
Retained image outputs can be republished without rerendering.

## Inspectable production evidence

After capture or review, a requested inspection export uses the same prepared sources, consumer, receipts and bytes through [Evidence Review](evidence-review.md).
Exporting a report or study is read-only with respect to production and canon.
Exported observations never authorize a new action; continue decisions through the authority-bearing workflow.
